RANsquawk Daily US Equity Opening News – 17th August 2018 – Earnings from AMAT, NVDA, DE Posted By: RanSquawk August 17, 2018
To download the report, please click here If you would like to subscribe to receive the research sheets directly in your inbox, you can now do so under the Research Suite section of the portal. To subscribe simply check the box next to “Email these reports” under the desired category.
17th August 2018
Earnings
Applied Materials Inc (AMAT) Q3 Adj. EPS USD 1.20 vs. Exp. USD 1.17, revenue USD 4.47bln vs. Exp. USD 4.43bln. Q3 gross margin 46.4% vs. Prev. 46.6%. CEO says FY18 to deliver double digit growth in all groups. Sees Q4 EPS USD 0.92 -1.00, consensus USD 1.17. Sees Q4 revenue USD 3.85bln-4.15bln, consensus USD 4.46bln. Sees FY18 EPS USD 4.41- 4.49, consensus USD 4.59, sees FY18 revenue USD 17.1bln -17.4bln, consensus USD 17.65bln. (Newswires) Deere & Co (DE) Q2 EPS USD 2.59 vs. Exp. USD 2.74, revenue USD 9.28bln vs. Exp. USD 9.21bln. Says they have continued to face cost pressures for raw materials and freight. Sees FY Adj. Net profit at USD 3.10bln vs. Exp. USD 3.17bln. Sees FY18 company worldwide agriculture & turf sales up approx. 15%. (Newswires) Nordstrom (JWN) Q2 EPS USD 0.95 vs. Exp. USD 0.84, revenue USD 3.98bln vs. Exp. USD 3.96bln. Raises FY18 EPS to USD 3.50- 3.65 from USD 3.35-3.55 and boosts FY18 revenue view to USD 15.4bln-USD 15.5bln from USD 15.2bln-15.4bln, consensus USD 15.78bln. (Newswires) NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) Q2 Adj. EPS USD 1.94 vs. Exp. USD 1.66, revenue USD 3.12bln vs. Exp. USD 3.1bln. Gaming revenue by 52% y/y to USD 1.80bln. Sees Q3 revenue USD 3.25bln, plus/minus 2%, consensus USD 3.34bln. (Newswires) Adtalem Global Education (ATGE) Q4 continuing operations EPS USD 0.86 vs. Exp. USD 0.91, revenue USD 0.319bln vs. Exp. USD 0.352bln. (Newswires) DJIA
Apple (AAPL) – The tech titan is set to be launching its entry-level MacBook series, which includes Intel’s (INTC) 14nm Kaby Lake processor, in the co.’s conference in September, the MacBook is likely to cost USD 1,200 sources report. Foxconn, Apple’s biggest supplier, is launching a semiconductor plant in China’s Pearl River Delta. Of note for Semiconductor names, (NXPI, AMAT, KLAC, INTC, QCOM) (Newswires/WSJ) Intel (INTC) – There are reports that the chip manufacturing giant has acquired the deep-learning startup Vertex.AI. The startup team will work alongside Intel’s Movidius team in its AI product group. (Newswires) McDonald’s (MCD) – The FDA provides an update on the Cyclospora illnesses case confirming it was reported in people consuming the restaurant’s salad and that it affected consumers in 15 states. (Newswires) Merck (MRK) – The healthcare group and Eisai (ESALY) announce the FDA has granted approval for LENVIMA capsules for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma. (Newswires) S&P500
Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. (BMY) – The FDA has approved Opdivo, the first new medication in almost 20 years for the treatment of small cell lung cancer; brought to the market by BMY. (Newswires) Express Scripts (ESRX) – The co. urges stockholders to vote in favour of the merger with Cigna (CI) at the upcoming 24th August special meeting. (Newswires) Mattel (MAT) – The co. names Steve Totzke as CCO. (Newswires) MetLife (MET) – The co. and State Street (STT) enter a multi-year USD 2bln commercial mortgage co-lending deal. (Newswires) Regeneron (REGN) – The FDA grants approval for EYLEA Injection in patients with wet age-related macular degeneration. (Newswires) Tyson Foods (TSN) – The co. acquires keystone from Brazil’s Mafrig for USD 2.5bln; according to sources. (Newswires) Twitter (TWTR) – US House panel is said to mull subpeona for CEO Dorsey, according to reports. (Politico) NASDAQ 100
Alphabet (GOOGL) – The co.’s CEO, Sundar Pichai, was said to have mentioned in a companywide meeting on Thursday that Google is not close to launching a Chinese search engine. Separately, the tech giant submitted plans for Moffett Park development, a major campus in based in Silicon Valley following its previously made USD 1bln investment in the area. (Newswires) Facebook (FB) – The social network stopped returning searches on opioids drugs. (Newswires) Tesla (TSLA) – The SEC is placing pressure on the automaker’s directors to understand how much details CEO Elon Musk shared with them prior to the announcement of his plan to take the co. private. Separately, workers at the Fremont facility, where Model 3 is assembled, were sent home 3.5 hours earlier on Wednesday without meeting their targets. Musk also has no plans to relinquish his CEO/Chairman roles in his companies, the NYT reported that people familiar to the matter have said that SpaceX could help take Tesla private. The co. is seen losing around USD 5,900 on every basic model 3, according to UBS. (WSJ/Business Insider/NYT) OTHER NEWS
Etsy (ETSY) – Chairman Frederick Wilson sells USD 1mln in common stock. (Newswires) Scientific Games (SGMS) – The co. and Pennsylvania Lottery launched virtual sports at retailers across the US. (Newswires) SJW Corp. (SJW) – The co. rejected the revised USD 70/shr offer made by California Water Service (CTWS). (Newswires) Toyota (TM) – The car producer said it will increase its capacity in its China Guangzhou plant and expand its production by 120,000 vehicles per year in its Tianjin factory. (Newswires) BROKER MOVES
